Statistical methods and populations
Reference distributions retain their source population when filtering. Intervals are supplied values; filtering does not recalculate them.


Point at a mark to inspect its row ID.




Source observations


Original simulated intensity image and labels by Mark Marosi · MIT material. These shapes are a visualization fixture, not observed cells or an inferred segmentation. Area counts labeled source pixels using the declared calibration. Mean and minimum–maximum use nonmissing labeled intensities; ranges are not confidence intervals. The source image stays visible during filtering; region outlines, picking and plot marks follow visibility. Python measured the axes and outlined text. This prototype renders circles, line segments, bars and polygon regions with fixed page geometry, clips them to their plot areas and preserves row identity. Page zoom moves the whole drawing; it does not recalculate domains or ticks. Data and runtime are embedded for offline use.
